messages:
alex: Heads up — saw duplicated token sequences when running long-window QA against the new 4-bit quant build. Repro is consistent when context > 32768 and KV cache is used across chunk boundaries.

alex: Minimal repro:
```bash
python tests/kv_repro.py --model redwood/gptx-7b-4bit --seq 65536 --chunk 4096 --prompt tests/long_prompt.txt
```

alex: Log excerpt around duplication point:
```
[2026-01-12 14:03:21] TOK 32760: "...the previous paragraph."
[2026-01-12 14:03:21] TOK 32761: "Reproduced start"
[2026-01-12 14:03:21] TOK 32762: "Reproduced start"  <-- duplicate
[2026-01-12 14:03:21] TOK 32763: "continuation..."
```

tara: Oof. Does this happen on single-GPU local runtime or only on multi-shard dedicated pools?

alex: Reproduced locally (single GPU) and in dedicated canary. Seems tied to: quantized weights + continuous KV caching + when RoPE scaling crosses the wrap threshold.

mina: Hypothesis: cached k/v are being reused with stale positional rotation. If we store rotated KV instead of raw and then reapply rotation per-chunk, we could double-rotate. Also possible mismatch between the position offset used when writing vs when reading cache.

ryan: Can you dump the pos_ids we pass when writing to cache vs when reading? If the write uses absolute positions and the read expects chunk-relative, that would explain duplications.

alex: I dumped the position meta. Write: pos_start=0, pos_end=32768; Read when serving next chunk: pos_offset=32768 but runtime applies RoPE multiply with pos_idx starting at 0 again. So keys get rotated twice for tokens near boundary.

mina: That matches. Two actionable fixes: 1) store raw KV (no rotation) and apply RoPE at read-time with correct offset OR 2) ensure stored KV also has metadata about applied rotation and skip reapplying. First is simpler but may change perf.

ryan: Quick experiment request: run parity test with kv_rotation_mode toggled. Use these two flags we added: `--kv-rotate-on-write` (default true) and `--kv-rotate-on-read`. Compare output hashes.

alex: Ran both modes. Results:
- kv-rotate-on-write=true, kv-rotate-on-read=false => duplication reproduced.
- kv-rotate-on-write=false, kv-rotate-on-read=true => no duplication, matches baseline non-quantized outputs.

alex: So the bug is interaction between pre-rotated cached KV + read-time rotation being applied again. But why appears only with 4-bit quant and long contexts?

mina: Possible explanation: quantized kernels do fused RoPE in matmul path for perf (we added an optimization in runtime/quant_kernels.cu that assumes unrotated KV). If cache contains rotated KV, the fused kernel applies extra rotation implicitly. With full precision those fused paths aren't used, so it doesn't surface.

ryan: That explains it. Action items:
- revert fused RoPE assumption in quant path OR add a flag to opt-out when cache metadata indicates pre-rotated.
- add unit test for chunk boundary duplication with seq lengths 32768, 65536.

alex: I'll open a PR with a conservative fix: make fused kernel check a `kv_rotated` header before doing implicit rotation. Patch here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/789 (WIP)

devops-bot: CI job started: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/long-kv/342 (runs long-window smoke)

tara: Also add an eval to longbench-suite that compares token-level diff counts for the same seed across quant variants. We should gate canaries on >0 dups per 100k tokens.

mina: I'll push a unit test into tests/long_context/test_cache_rotation.py with two small cases and a randomized fuzz run (seeded).

alex: For the immediate canary: I'll deploy a patch that forces `--kv-rotate-on-write=false` for the 4-bit canary image and roll to 1% traffic. If the canary is clean after 24h we can merge the kernel guard.

ryan: Postmortem notes for release doc: root cause = mismatch between cached KV rotation semantics and fused quantized RoPE kernel. Impact = duplicated tokens near chunk boundary for very long contexts when using quantized runtimes. Workaround = disable rotate-on-write for 4-bit images.

tara: Thanks — assign me to coordinate canary and change request with SRE. @devops-bot can you schedule the 1% rollout tomorrow 09:00 PT?

devops-bot: Scheduled canary rollout: 2026-01-13 09:00 PT. Job: https://deploy.redwood.ai/canary/987

alex: Quick note — benchmark numbers: with kv-rotate-on-read true the 4-bit path is ~5% slower on token throughput vs current production, but correctness is prioritized. We'll optimize later.

mina: Good. I'll follow up with a micro-optimization to keep fused path but respect `kv_rotated` flag.

alex: Thanks everyone. I'll update the PR with unit test and results from the 1% canary tomorrow. :thumbsup:

ryan: Appreciate it.
